source_anchor: CRITICAL LESSON: HTTP 200 ≠ Homepage Is Working
instance: Homepage pod showed Running and the service returned HTTP 200, but every widget on the rendered page displayed "API Error" text; standard HTTP status and pod-health checks passed while the app was functionally broken.
check: Download the actual HTML (not just the status code) and grep it for the string "API Error"; must return empty.

source_anchor: CRITICAL LESSON: Widget Functionality Can Break Silently
instance: Proxmox widget lost its dynamic functionality (no CPU/memory/storage stats shown) after a configuration change, while HTTP 200 held, logs showed no errors, and the widget still rendered on the page.
check: After any config change, open Homepage in a browser and confirm the Proxmox widget shows live CPU/memory/storage stats rather than dashes/zeros.

source_anchor: CRITICAL LESSON: Widget Functionality Can Break Silently
instance: Both Pihole widgets lost dynamic functionality (no query counts or blocking stats) after a configuration change, with no HTTP errors or log errors surfacing the failure.
check: After any config change, verify both Pihole widgets show live DNS query metrics, not static/placeholder data.

source_anchor: CRITICAL LESSON: Favicon Loading Must Be Verified
instance: Automatic favicon fetching (URL-based icon: pointing at each service's /favicon.ico) produced broken/incorrect icons for LinkedIn, Perplexity, Linkerd, and Dashlane, due to missing standard favicon locations and CORS/CSP restrictions.
check: After adding/changing services, open Homepage in a browser, verify all service icons load, and check the browser network tab for favicon 404s; prefer icon libraries (mdi-*, si-*) over URL-based icons.

source_anchor: CRITICAL LESSON: Search Widget Configuration Must Be Exact
instance: Search widget config was changed from a working `provider: custom` with full `/search?q=` URL to `provider: searxng` with a bare base URL, which produced a "Something went wrong" error on every search.
check: Confirm configmap shows `provider: custom` with a URL including `/search?q=`, and test an actual search in the browser after any change to this config.

source_anchor: Core Issues Identified > 1. Using :latest Tag Instead of Pinned Versions
instance: Running Homepage on the `:latest` image tag silently pulled v1.7.0, which introduced a new hard requirement for a `proxmox.yaml` file and shipped a buggy ingress API client that produced `NaN undefined undefined` errors, breaking a previously-working deployment without any explicit version-change action.
check: Grep deployment manifests for `image:.*:latest` before applying; image tag must be a pinned, tested version.

source_anchor: Core Issues Identified > 2. Kubernetes Auto-Discovery Mode Enabled by Default
instance: `kubernetes.yaml` defaulted to `mode: cluster`, causing Homepage to poll the Kubernetes API (listing ingresses roughly every 3 seconds across all namespaces) even when no kubernetes widget was explicitly configured; incomplete RBAC or API-format changes turned this into continuous error-log spam that obscured real issues.
check: Grep `kubernetes.yaml` for an explicit `mode:` setting (`disabled` if the feature isn't in use) rather than relying on the default; watch logs for repeating errors at ~3s cadence, which indicates polling.

source_anchor: Core Issues Identified > 3. Widget Configuration Inconsistency
instance: A Proxmox widget was defined in services.yaml (type: proxmox, url set) with no corresponding proxmox.yaml file mounted in the deployment, causing the widget to fail to initialize.
check: For every widget type referenced in services/widgets config, confirm its required config file (e.g. proxmox.yaml, docker.yaml) is present in the ConfigMap and mounted via volumeMounts before deploying.

source_anchor: Core Issues Identified > 4. Insufficient Error Analysis Before Making Changes
instance: During one debugging session, API errors were addressed by changing icons (unrelated), then the image version (partial fix), then disabling node metrics (incomplete) — three wrong fixes applied in sequence before disabling kubernetes mode, the actual root cause, was tried last.
check: Before changing anything, collect and bucket error patterns from logs (kubectl logs | grep error | sort | uniq -c) and identify the specific failing component before making a targeted fix.

source_anchor: Core Issues Identified > 5. Not Preserving Known-Good Configurations
instance: Homepage was working with zero errors, then a security-hardening change broke it, and there was no backed-up configuration or git tag of the prior working state to revert to, making the regression hard to diagnose or undo.
check: Backup the current ConfigMap/manifest (timestamped copy or git tag) before applying any change.

source_anchor: Common Homepage Errors and Fixes > Error: ECONNREFUSED to Proxmox/Service
instance: A widget's backend service was unreachable from the Homepage pod's network, producing ECONNREFUSED, because connectivity from the pod to the target service had not been verified before the widget was added.
check: Test network connectivity (curl/nc) from the pod's network to a widget's backend URL before enabling that widget.

source_anchor: Common Homepage Errors and Fixes > Error: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'items')
instance: An installed Homepage version returned an API response whose shape didn't match what the code expected, producing "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'items')"; this was a version-specific bug rather than a configuration error.
check: Pin versions and test any version upgrade in a non-production namespace before rolling it to prod.
